question.problem:
The Taylor series for the function $f(x)$ about $x=0$ is given by 

$$
f(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{n}}{(2n+1)!}.
$$

Find the series expansion of ${f}^{′}(x).$

${f}^{′}(x)={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }$
{{field-1}}
$(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{n-1}$
question.worked_solution:
Writing the terms of the series explicitly, we have

$$
f(x)=\frac{x}{6}-\frac{{x}^{2}}{120}+⋯+{{\frac{(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{n}}{(2n+1)!}}_{⏟}}_{\text{the }n\text{th term}}+⋯.
$$

Differentiating the above series term-by-term gives

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=\frac{1}{6}-\frac{2x}{120}+⋯+{{\frac{(-1)^{n+1}n{x}^{n-1}}{(2n+1)!}}_{⏟}}_{\text{the }n\text{th term}}+⋯.
$$

We can now write the Taylor series for ${f}^{′}(x)$ using the sigma notation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(x) & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{n(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{n-1}}{(2n+1)!} \\  & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{n}{(2n+1)!}(-1)^{n+1}{x}^{n-1}\end{aligned}
$$
